quiz.title: Quiz Arena starter bank
quiz.description: Fifty questions across science, geography, history and India, ready to import.

questions.prompt: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.explanation: Mercury orbits at roughly 58 million km from the Sun, closer than any other planet.

questions.prompt: How many players from one team are on the field during a football match?
questions.explanation: Each side fields eleven players, one of whom is the goalkeeper.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Pacific covers about a third of the planet's surface, more than all the land put together.

questions.prompt: What is the capital of Australia?
questions.explanation: Canberra was purpose-built as a compromise capital between Sydney and Melbourne.

questions.prompt: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
questions.explanation: Au comes from aurum, the Latin word for gold; Ag is silver.

questions.prompt: Which gas do plants take in during photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Plants combine carbon dioxide and water using light energy, and release oxygen.

questions.prompt: In which country is the Taj Mahal?
questions.explanation: It stands in Agra, Uttar Pradesh, on the bank of the Yamuna.

questions.prompt: How many minutes long is a standard football match, excluding stoppage time?
questions.explanation: Two halves of 45 minutes each, with added time for stoppages.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest living land animal?
questions.explanation: A large bull African elephant can weigh over six tonnes.

questions.prompt: What does “www” stand for in a web address?
questions.explanation: Tim Berners-Lee named his hypertext system the World Wide Web in 1989.

questions.prompt: Which Indian city is called the “Silicon Valley of India”?
questions.explanation: Bengaluru's concentration of software firms earned it the nickname.

questions.prompt: How many days are there in a leap year?
questions.explanation: The extra day, 29 February, keeps the calendar aligned with Earth's orbit.

questions.prompt: Which colour appears at the top of a rainbow?
questions.explanation: Red has the longest wavelength, so it bends least and sits on the outer edge.

questions.prompt: What is the currency of Japan?
questions.explanation: The yen is Japan's currency; the won is Korean and the ringgit Malaysian.

questions.prompt: Which vitamin does the body make when skin is exposed to sunlight?
questions.explanation: Ultraviolet light triggers vitamin D synthesis in the skin.

questions.prompt: Which river runs through the Grand Canyon?
questions.explanation: The Colorado has been cutting the canyon in Arizona for about six million years.

questions.prompt: Who wrote “On the Origin of Species”?
questions.explanation: Darwin published it in 1859, setting out evolution by natural selection.

questions.prompt: Which element has atomic number 26?
questions.explanation: Iron sits at 26 on the periodic table, between manganese and cobalt.

questions.prompt: The Great Barrier Reef lies off the coast of which country?
questions.explanation: It stretches more than 2,300 km along the Queensland coast.

questions.prompt: Which Indian state has the longest coastline?
questions.explanation: Gujarat's coastline runs about 1,600 km along the Arabian Sea.

questions.prompt: How many balls are bowled in a standard over in cricket?
questions.explanation: An over is six legal deliveries; wides and no-balls do not count.

questions.prompt: Who was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize?
questions.explanation: Marie Curie shared the 1903 physics prize and later won chemistry in 1911.

questions.prompt: Which planet is home to the Great Red Spot?
questions.explanation: It is a storm wider than Earth that has been observed for centuries.

questions.prompt: Which is the hardest naturally occurring mineral?
questions.explanation: Diamond scores a perfect 10 on the Mohs hardness scale.

questions.prompt: Which country gave the Statue of Liberty to the United States?
questions.explanation: France presented it in 1886 to mark the centenary of American independence.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest hot desert in the world?
questions.explanation: The Sahara covers roughly 9 million square kilometres of North Africa.

questions.prompt: Which organ produces insulin?
questions.explanation: Beta cells in the pancreas release insulin to regulate blood sugar.

questions.prompt: In which year did India become independent?
questions.explanation: India became independent on 15 August 1947; the republic followed in 1950.

questions.prompt: Which language has the most native speakers in the world?
questions.explanation: Mandarin has close to a billion native speakers, ahead of Spanish.

questions.prompt: What is the chemical formula for table salt?
questions.explanation: Sodium chloride, NaCl, is the compound in everyday table salt.

questions.prompt: Which ocean trench contains the deepest known point on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench lies almost 11 km below the surface.

questions.prompt: Mount Kilimanjaro is in which country?
questions.explanation: Kilimanjaro rises in northern Tanzania near the Kenyan border.

questions.prompt: Who set out the three laws of motion?
questions.explanation: Newton published the laws in Principia Mathematica in 1687.

questions.prompt: What does DNA stand for?
questions.explanation: The name describes the sugar deoxyribose and the acid backbone of the molecule.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest Indian state by area?
questions.explanation: Rajasthan covers about 342,000 square kilometres, the most of any state.

questions.prompt: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
questions.explanation: Leonardo painted it in Florence in the early sixteenth century.

questions.prompt: What is the smallest prime number?
questions.explanation: 2 is prime because it has exactly two factors, 1 and itself; 1 has only one.

questions.prompt: Which blood type is known as the universal donor?
questions.explanation: O negative red cells carry no A, B or RhD antigens to trigger a reaction.

questions.prompt: In which city is the United Nations headquartered?
questions.explanation: The UN headquarters has stood on Manhattan's East River since 1952.

questions.prompt: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Mercury melts at about minus 39 degrees Celsius, so it stays liquid indoors.

questions.prompt: Which element is the most abundant in Earth's crust by mass?
questions.explanation: Oxygen makes up roughly 46 percent of the crust by mass, mostly bound in minerals.

questions.prompt: In which year was the Treaty of Versailles signed?
questions.explanation: It was signed on 28 June 1919, formally ending the First World War with Germany.

questions.prompt: Who wrote the “Aryabhatiya”?
questions.explanation: Aryabhata wrote the Aryabhatiya in 499 CE, covering astronomy and mathematics.

questions.prompt: Which subatomic particle was discovered first?
questions.explanation: J J Thomson identified the electron in 1897, decades before the proton and neutron.

questions.prompt: What was the name of the lander on India's Chandrayaan-3 mission?
questions.explanation: Vikram landed near the lunar south pole in August 2023; Pragyan was its rover.

questions.prompt: Which country spans the most time zones, counting its overseas territories?
questions.explanation: France reaches twelve time zones through its overseas departments and territories.

questions.prompt: Which strait separates Asia from North America?
questions.explanation: The Bering Strait runs between Russia's Chukotka and Alaska.

questions.prompt: What is the SI unit of electrical resistance?
questions.explanation: One ohm is the resistance that passes one ampere under one volt.

questions.prompt: Which two countries share the longest land border in the world?
questions.explanation: Their shared border runs about 8,890 km, including the Alaska section.

questions.prompt: Which is the only mammal capable of true flight?
questions.explanation: Only bats have powered flight; the others glide.
